ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r5.claim: Immediate revelation reassures Moses that he will remain dominant however profound the magic seems.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p48/r5.anchor: he will remain dominant come what may

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r5.claim: إنك أنت الأعلى emphatically promises Moses victory and overpowering through a renewed clause, إن, repeated pronoun, definiteness, and the superlative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p356/r5.anchor: إنك أنت الأعلى تقرير لغلبته وقهره وتوكيد بالاستئناف وبكلمة التوكيد وبتكرير الضمير وبلام التعريف، وبالأعلوية الدالة على التفضيل

TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r3.claim: God's command not to fear is meant to strengthen and support Moses: because he is superior to them in every respect, their trick cannot harm him.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#9/r3.anchor: نهي بداعي التقوية والتأييد وقد علله بقوله { انك أنت الأعلى } فالمعنى انك فوقهم من كل جهة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r1.claim: God tells Moses not to remain afraid of what he imagined and to dispel the fear that had overcome him; the prohibition is literal.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r1.anchor: أي لاتستمر على خوفك مما توهمت وادفع عن نفسك ما اعتراك فالنهى على حقيقته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r2.claim: Another view takes the prohibition as encouragement meant to strengthen Moses’ heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : حرج عن ذلك للتشجيع وتقوية القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r3.claim: The assurance explains why Moses should stop fearing and emphatically establishes his victory through a discourse response, affirmation, repeated pronoun, definite predicate, and comparative wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r3.anchor: تعليل لما يوجبه النهى من الأنتهاء عن الخوف وتقرير لغلبته على ابلغ وجه وآكده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī takes the comparative form as intensifying the assertion, not implying that the magicians also achieved manifest superiority; comparison with the onlookers is irrelevant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p228#3/r4.anchor: والذى أميل اليه أن الصيغة المذكورة لمجرد الزيارة فان كونها للمشاركة والزيادة يقتضى أن يكون للسحرة علو وغلبة ظاهرة أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p287#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says Moses feared for his people lest they lose their share of God, not for himself; “you are uppermost” means either guarded by divine care or victorious enough to make them followers.

BURSEVI:v5p309/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309/r7.claim: God tells Moses not to fear what he had imagined and reassures him that he is the one who will prevail over the magicians.
BURSEVI:v5p309/r7.anchor: ما توهمت {إنك} أي : لأنك {أنت الاعلى} أي : الغالب القاهر لهم

BURSEVI:v5p309/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p309/r8.claim: Moses prevails because God accompanies him in every state; Moses depends on the Causer, while the magicians depend on causes, and divine signs protect him.
BURSEVI:v5p309/r8.anchor: ونحن معك في جميع أحوالك فإنك القائم بالمسبب وهم القائمون المعتمدون على الأسباب وأيضا معك آياتنا الكبرى وهو لباس حفظنا

BURSEVI:v5p309/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p309/r9.claim: Human fear is embedded even in a prophet’s nature until God removes it through a divine command; Moses is too elevated to fear creatures rather than the Creator.
BURSEVI:v5p309/r9.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن خوف البشرية مركوز في جبلة الإنسان ولو كان نبيا إلى أن ينزع الله الخوف منه

BURSEVI:v5p309/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p309/r10.claim: The inward reading says Moses feared the Creator, not the staff: he recognized the serpent swallowing magic as a manifestation of God’s overpowering attribute.
BURSEVI:v5p309/r10.anchor: وفيه معنى آخر أن خوف موسى ما كان من المكونات بل من المكون إذ رأى عصاه ثعبانا تلقف سحر السحرة

BURSEVI:v5p309/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p309/r11.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p309/r11.claim: Moses is higher than his created staff as God’s messenger and chosen intimate, manifesting divine gentleness and power, while the staff manifested only overpowering.
BURSEVI:v5p309/r11.anchor: لأنك على درجة عندنا منها لأنها عصاك مصنوعة لنفسك وأنت رسولي وكليمي واصطنعتك لنفسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r8.claim: The emphatic إن, separating pronoun, and definite الأعلى show that Moses feared the magicians might seem to the public to prevail, even temporarily.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r8.anchor: فتأكيد الجملة بحرف التأكيد وتقوية تأكيدها بضمير الفصل وبالتعريف في { الأعلى } دليل على أن ما خامره من الخوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r9.claim: Although Moses was certain God would fulfill His mission, God could briefly let unbelievers prosper to test believers’ steadfastness, as stated in the warning about their worldly roaming.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p259/r9.anchor: كما قال لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم { لا يغرنك تقلب الذين كفروا في البلاد متاع قليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306/r1.claim: Moses is reassured that he will prevail over them through victory; Ibn al-Jawzi says this is more accurate than the first explanation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306/r1.anchor: لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى عليهم بالظفر والغلبة وهذا أصح من الأول

MUQATIL:20:64-68/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:64-68/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:64-68/r5.claim: Gabriel conveyed God's reassurance that Moses would be victor; Muqatil compares it with 3:139 and 47:35, where being uppermost means victorious.
MUQATIL:20:64-68/r5.anchor: هذا قول جبريل لموسى، عليه السلام، عن أمر ربه، عز وجل، وهو على يمينه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r1.claim: Al-aʿlā means the victor and dominant one.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r2.claim: The particle inna, the pronoun anta, the definite article, and the word al-ʿulūw intensify the assertion of manifest superiority.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60#5/r2.anchor: وفي ذكر أن وأنت وحرف التعريف ولفظ العلو وهو الغلبة الظاهرة مبالغة بينه

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r1.speaker: أكثر النحويين
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r1.claim: Most grammarians distinguish kalima, a single word, from kalam, a complete meaningful sentence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r1.anchor: قال أكثر النحويين : الكلمة غير الكلام فالكلمة هي اللفظة المفردة

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r2.speaker: أكثر الأصوليين
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r2.claim: Most legal theorists see no distinction: both kalima and kalam can denote a simple word or a compound expression.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r2.anchor: وقال أكثر الأصوليين إنه لا فرق بينهما فكل واحد منهما يتناول المفرد والمركب

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r3.speaker: ابن جني
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r3.claim: Ibn Jinni agrees with the grammarians and regards the theologians' position as unlikely.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r3.anchor: وابن جني وافق النحويين واستبعد قول المتكلمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r4.claim: Razi finds Ibn Jinni's proof weak; it chiefly relies on a Sibawayh passage suggesting kalam is restricted to a complete sentence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r4.anchor: وما رأيت في كلامه حجة قوية في الفرق سوى أنه نقل عن سيبويه كلاما مشعر

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r5.speaker: أكثر الأصوليين
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r5.claim: They argue a single word is speech because it opposes silence, effects understanding (the root kalm means wound or effect), can be called speaking in ordinary usage, and can be called incomplete speech without complete benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r5.anchor: أما الأصوليون فقد احتجوا على صحة قولهم بوجوه الأول : أن العقلاء قد اتفقوا على أن الكلام ما يضاد

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r6.claim: The semantic dispute creates an oath-law question discussed first in Muhammad ibn al-Hasan's al-Jamiʿ al-Kabir: a man makes his unconsummated wife divorced three times if he speaks to her.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r6.anchor: تفرع على الاختلاف المذكور مسألة فقهية وهي أولى مسائل أيمان الجامع الكبير لمحمد بن الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة وصاحباه
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa and his two companions rule that the second utterance of the conditional phrase effects one divorce.

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r8.speaker: زفر
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r8.claim: Zufar rules that the second utterance does not effect a divorce.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r8.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة وصاحباه : تنعقد وقال زفر : لا تنعقد

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r9.speaker: زفر
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r9.claim: Zufar says the condition is met as soon as the speaker says “if I speak to you,” since kalam includes any meaningful utterance; the following divorce clause then falls outside the marriage and is ineffective.
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r9.anchor: وحجة زفر أنه لما قال في المرة الثانية إن كلمتك فعند هذا القدر من الكلام حصل الشرط

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa holds the condition incomplete until the full sentence is spoken, so the divorce takes effect only at the end of “if I speak to you, you are divorced.”
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r10.anchor: وحجة أبي حنيفة أن الشرط - وهو قوله إن كلمتك - غير تام والكلام اسم للجملة التامة

RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p26/r11.claim: Razi notes that if the man says “whenever I speak to you” and stops at the second occurrence, the repetition particle seems to entail three divorces under the single-word definition; he suggests Zufar may accept this result.

SULAMI:v1p446#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p446#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p446#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says Moses need not fear because God sees and hears him and is with him; Moses relies on the Causer while his opponents depend on material causes.
SULAMI:v1p446#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ' لا تخف فإنك بمرأى منا

THALABI:v6p252/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r12.claim: God's reassurance that Moses is al-aʿlā means that he is the victor.
THALABI:v6p252/r12.anchor: قلنا لموسى لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى الغالب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “you are the highest” as “you are the victor.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r1.anchor: فقال الله تعالى: {لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى} قال ابن عباس: (يريد أنت الغالب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r2.claim: Moses is above them through victory and triumph.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p459/r2.anchor: والمعنى: أنت الأعلى عليهم بالظفر والغلبة.

BURHAN:v1p49/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p49/r1.claim: A connection between passages need not be of one specific kind; any relation suffices, and the aim here is to affirm the Qur'an, urge acting on it, and encourage faith before the discourse returns to its opening.
BURHAN:v1p49/r1.anchor: قلنا لا يشترط فى الجامع ذلك بل يكفى التعلق على أى وجه كان ويكفى فى وجه الربط ما ذكرنا

TABRISI:20:71-72/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r15.claim: God reassures Moses that he will prevail over the magicians through victory and dominance.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r15.anchor: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى } عليهم بالظفر والغلبة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r8.claim: God reassures Moses that he will prevail.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r8.anchor: لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى } الغالب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r7.claim: Moses feared inwardly, but God told him he would be the manifest victor.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r7.anchor: {فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى {67} قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى {68} } [طه: 67-68] الظاهر.

QASHANI:20:64-70/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r5.claim: God's reassurance strengthens Moses through the Holy Spirit.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r5.anchor: { قلنا لا تخف } شجعناه وأيدناه، بروح القدس

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r14.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r14.claim: The magicians' spectacle seemed to affect Moses briefly, making him fear that the people would be taken in, but God's reassurance raised his morale.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r14.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın dahi bir an için etkilenip insanların buna kapılmalarından endişe duyduğu (İbn Atıyye, IV, 51-52), fakat Allah’ın gerçeği bildirmesiyle mâneviyatının yükseltildiği

NAHHAS:v3p48/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p48/r11.claim: God reassures Moses that the apparent confusion will be clarified and that he will prevail by proof.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r11.anchor: أي لا تخف الشبه فإنا سنبين أمرك حتى تعلو عليهم بالبرهان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r1.claim: Moses is assured that he will prevail and win.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r1.anchor: {قلنا} لموسى: {لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى} أي: الغالب، يعني: لك الغلبة والظفر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r2.claim: God's assurance that Moses is uppermost explains the command not to fear and emphasizes victory through independent assertion, certainty particle, repeated pronoun, definite predicate, and superlative wording.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:67-69/r2.anchor: تعليل للنهي وتقرير لغلبته مؤكدا بالاستئناف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r1.claim: Since God was with Moses and could nullify the magic, He reassured him not to fear any part of their affair.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r2.claim: The emphatic wording answers the expectation that the impressive magic might prevail: Moses alone would be manifestly victorious.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29/r2.anchor: أي خاصة { الأعلى * } أي الغالب غلبة ظاهرة لا شبهة فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r4.claim: The declaration means that Moses will prevail over whoever opposes him in this contest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52/r4.anchor: أي الغالب لمن ناوأك في هذا المقام

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412#2/r10.claim: God's reassurance steadied Moses and removed his fear.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r1.claim: Moses objected to Gabriel's call for gentleness because the magicians sought to defeat the miracle and support Pharaoh's religion; Gabriel said they would be with Moses until afternoon prayer and then in Paradise.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r2.claim: Moses wondered whether God's knowledge of him might differ from his present state, as it had with the magicians; God then reassured him not to fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r2.anchor: فلعلي أكون الآن في حالة، وعلم الله في على خلافها كما كان هؤلاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r3.claim: Moses is highest in that he prevails over the magicians in this world and holds the highest ranks in Paradise through prophethood and God's choosing him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r3.anchor: أي الغالب لهم في الدنيا، وفي الدرجات العلا في الجنة للنبوة والاصطفاء الذي آتاك الله به

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r12.claim: The general reassurance that Moses is “the higher” removes fear that his case will fail to prevail.
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r12.anchor: ودلالته على أن خوفه كان لأمر يرجع إلى أن أمره لا يظهر للقوم فآمنه الله تعالى بقوله : { إنك أنت الأعلى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p72#2/r13.speaker: author
